poc_summary: Custom-crafted 317-byte EXR file (poc8.exr) with a "channels" chlist attribute containing an "uncommon" channel combination (only "R" is a recognized single-letter channel; a preceding 19-byte crafted pseudo-channel entry supplies raw bytes that double as an absolute file offset once decode_header mis-handles the error path), width=64/height=1, compression=ZIP1, one scanline block with a small valid zlib-compressed payload. Run identically on every revision with: `/work/ffmpeg -y -loglevel error -i $INPUT -f rawvideo -pix_fmt gbrpf32le /tmp/out.raw`.
explanation: The intro commit (6e8cf0377fee) adds a new "uncommon channel combination" validation in decode_header() but writes `ret = AVERROR(AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME);` — wrapping the already-negative AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME constant in the AVERROR() negation macro a second time, turning it positive (this is the labelled LogicError: an inverted/incorrect error-sign check). Callers only treat `ret < 0` as failure, so this positive "error" is silently treated as success. Additionally, the early `goto fail` on this path skips the line that normally re-syncs the header's GetByteContext past the channels attribute (`gb->buffer = ch_gb.buffer + 1; continue;`), so decode_frame proceeds with the header cursor stuck mid-way through the channel list and with an incomplete channel_offsets array (two of R/G/B left at -1, since only "R" was a recognized channel name in my PoC). decode_block then computes channel_buffer pointers as `src + xsize*channel_offsets[i]`, and for the unassigned channels (-1) this points 4*xsize bytes before the start of the freshly-allocated per-line buffer; reading from it is a heap-buffer-overflow READ, reproducing the linked OSS-Fuzz report (UNKNOWN READ in decode_block via avcodec_default_execute2/decode_frame). This logic bug's observable consequence is the memory-safety violation, so I verified it with a sanitizer oracle as the instructions allow ("a sanitizer ... report can establish the observed regression even when the task's bug-type label is imprecise"). I verified end-to-end in Docker: the crafted poc8.exr reproduces a clean AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ only on post_intro (6e8cf0377fee); the byte-identical file run with the byte-identical command on pre_intro (dd092f7fd966, lacks the new check, rejects the file safely via a different, pre-existing path) and on post_benign (fix commit applied, restores the negative return so decode_frame correctly aborts before decode_block) both terminate cleanly with exit 69 and no crash/no sanitizer report. This satisfies the required invariant of a single reproducer that crashes only in post_intro.

Allocation trace shows the 712-byte region was allocated in decode_block exr.c:1387 (av_fast_padded_malloc) in the very same decode_frame call, i.e. an OOB read just before the freshly-allocated per-scanline decompression buffer.
pre_intro: identical poc8.exr + identical command cleanly fails with "Invalid data found when processing input" (exit 69, no crash, 0 frames decoded) — the pre-intro code lacks the new channel-combination check entirely and rejects the malformed channel set through a different, correctly-negative error path (no ASAN report at all).
post_benign: identical poc8.exr + identical command cleanly fails with "Not yet implemented in FFmpeg, patches welcome" (exit 69, no crash, no ASAN report) — i.e. AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME is now correctly propagated as negative, so decode_frame's `if (ret < 0) return ret;` check catches it and aborts before decode_block runs.
